questions.q: What problem does a standard memo line solve?
options: It gives ad hoc charges and credits a reusable description and default accounting, instead of free text and manual GL coding
It replaces the need for customer accounts
It automatically applies receipts to invoices
It calculates tax on standard invoices only
questions.explain: Memo lines exist for ad hoc billing scenarios (debit memos, credits, chargebacks) that don't come from a catalog or price list.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a place memo lines are typically used?
options: Debit memos
A standard invoice line sourced from a price list
On-account credits
Chargebacks
questions.explain: Standard invoice lines usually come from a price list or project billing data, not from a memo line; memo lines are for the ad hoc scenarios.

questions.q: Besides a description, what does a memo line default?
options: The customer's credit limit
The company's ledger currency
Accounting references for AutoAccounting, tax classification, and optionally a unit price
The transaction source
questions.explain: A memo line can default accounting references, a tax classification, and in some cases a fixed unit price, in addition to its description.

questions.q: In the restocking fee example, what did selecting the 'Restocking Fee' memo line accomplish?
options: It merged Harborline's duplicate customer record
It automatically wrote off the fee
It created a new transaction type
It filled in the standardized description and defaulted the correct GL account and tax classification automatically
questions.explain: The memo line's defaults meant the clerk didn't need to type a description or manually choose an account — it applied consistently every time.

questions.q: Why does consistency matter when using memo lines across a business?
options: So the same type of ad hoc charge (like a restocking fee) always posts to the same account regardless of who enters it or which customer it's billed to
It doesn't matter; each person can account for a charge however they like
Because memo lines are only used once and then deleted
Because tax rates change daily
questions.explain: The whole value of a memo line is that it standardizes how a recurring, ad hoc kind of charge or credit is described and accounted for.
